articleTitle: Temporal and frequency analysis of power signatures for common household appliances
publicationTitle: Symposium on ICT and Energy Efficiency and Workshop on Information Theory and Security (CIICT 2012)
abstract: This paper proposes a characterisation method of using electrical signal analysis to identify appliances. A low cost current sensor is used to measure an electrical load signal. The measured signal's transient and steady states are analysed in both the temporal and frequency domains. A signature is then derived from this analysis. From the methods used in the paper it is shown that appliances can be clearly identified and classified.

articleTitle: Ant colony system based clustering routing algorithm for large-scale wireless sensor networks
publicationTitle: Symposium on ICT and Energy Efficiency and Workshop on Information Theory and Security (CIICT 2012)
abstract: Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) have received a lot of attentions recently due to their wide applications. The major motivation to improve the routing performance of wireless sensor networks is due to the constraints of energy supplying and computation, especially for the large-scale WSNs. So an ant colony system based clustering routing algorithm is presented. Firstly the network is clustered into some small-scale regional clusters according to the distribution characteristics of the nodes. Then it applies the ant colony system algorithm parallel to search for the optimal path for each region cluster and determines the centers of the region clusters. Finally it forms the optimal data transmission paths according to the optimal regional path solutions and the sequence of the centers of the region clusters by applying the ant system again. It greatly improves the computational performance and gives an important inspiration to the routing establishment to large-scale wireless sensor networks by decomposing the global solution of the whole task into the sub-problems' solutions according to the clustering features applying the ant colony system. The time complexity analysis and simulations show the good performance of the algorithm.

articleTitle: A speaker recognition system based on MFCC and SCHMM
publicationTitle: Symposium on ICT and Energy Efficiency and Workshop on Information Theory and Security (CIICT 2012)
abstract: Speaker recognition is a speaker identification technology based on physiological and behavioural characteristics of speaker's voice. HMM is a commonly used method in speaker recognition, which includes DHMM, CHMM and SCHMM. However, DHMM has a low accuracy and CHMM is too complex to compute. To overcome shortcomings of DHMM and CHMM, SCHMM, as a mixture of DHMM and CHMM, is a good choice. In this paper, a speaker recognition system based on MFCC and SCHMM will be discussed.

articleTitle: Acquisition and tracking loops based on software defined radio
publicationTitle: Symposium on ICT and Energy Efficiency and Workshop on Information Theory and Security (CIICT 2012)
abstract: Navigation receiver is the equipment that can measuring position, velocity and time with navigation signals at any time. Traditional navigation receiver is based on application-specific hardware, which has a high sensitivity and signal processing speed, but the flexibility is poor, once confirmed it can not be changed. In contrast, the navigation software receiver based on software defined radio (SDR) technology has many advantages, e.g. agility, easy to upgrade, and so on. So SDR receives a lot of attention and the area of application is more and more widely. Aiming at studying the receiver technologies, we have developed a GPS software receiver. In our application, a FFT based acquisition is used together with a fine frequency estimation method. A widely used PLL+DLL structure is applied in the tracking process. These entire algorithms are based on “block-process” to achieve good efficiency. Base on this receiver, others can research and approve new acquisition and tracking arithmetic.

articleTitle: A method for selective SVM integration based on cultural algorithm and negative correlation learning
publicationTitle: Symposium on ICT and Energy Efficiency and Workshop on Information Theory and Security (CIICT 2012)
abstract: In this paper, a method for selective SVM integration is introduced in order to improve the generalization performance of SVM, which is based on cultural algorithm and negative correlation learning. This method mainly includes four parts: independent sub-SVMs training by bootstrap technology, creating an adaptation function based on negative correlation learning, computing the optimal weight of SVM in the weighted average values, and SVM integration with the weighted value which is more than a given threshold value. In the experiments, this is an efficient and effective method to improve the generalization performance of SVM.

articleTitle: An improved algorithm of network reliability based on pathset and boolean operation
publicationTitle: Symposium on ICT and Energy Efficiency and Workshop on Information Theory and Security (CIICT 2012)
abstract: As we all know, the calculation of network reliability is a typical NP-hard problem. The method of calculating network reliability using pathset matrix and boolean operation is simple and easy to program. However, there exists a serious combinatorial explosion problem with the increasing complexity of a network. And the research of this method is just limited to the achievement more than improving efficiency. This paper starts with the pathset matrix and improves the efficiency form decreasing the memory utilization and redundancy. Some examples are given to prove the efficiency of the improve algorithm. And the efficiency of the improved algorithm is illustrated by examples.

articleTitle: A distributed real time sensor network for enhancing energy efficiency through ICT
publicationTitle: Symposium on ICT and Energy Efficiency and Workshop on Information Theory and Security (CIICT 2012)
abstract: The deployment of a sensor network plays an important role in implementation of the smart grid. An integrated sensor system is proposed in this paper, which is built with an Information and Communication Technology (ICT) structure. A functional wind monitoring sensor network and an indoor environment monitoring sensor network are described from a design and implementation aspect. With the concern of energy efficiency, a Multiple Access Control (MAC) mechanism is designed for a ZigBee network and a UDP-based communication strategy is used to achieve a high sampling frequency. Additionally, multiple energy-aware programming skills are talked from a practical aspect, as well as an energy harvesting strategy and a power consumption survey of this system. Based on the data gained by the system, initial data analysis and visualisation results are also presented.

articleTitle: Allocation of cloud storage based on improved genetic algorithm
publicationTitle: Symposium on ICT and Energy Efficiency and Workshop on Information Theory and Security (CIICT 2012)
abstract: With respect to the storage allocation of cloud storage, this paper presents a new method to solve the problem based on improved genetic algorithm. The model is the storage efficiency of cloud storage systems as the goal, to achieve load balancing, high efficient and storage security. Firstly, preprocess the storage tasks and nodes during the storage task allocation, and manage virtual tasks and nodes after preprocessing in a whole. And then apply the natural number encoding to encode the storage task, combine with storage efficiency matrix for the individual choice, and improve the crossover operator and mutation operator. Simulation results show that this strategy can achieve the cloud storage allocation effectively.

articleTitle: Low complexity synchronization in TD-SCDMA systems
publicationTitle: Symposium on ICT and Energy Efficiency and Workshop on Information Theory and Security (CIICT 2012)
abstract: At present, wireless communication technology is rapidly evolving to the 4G technology. Based on the physical frame structure of TD-LTE technology being same to TD-SCDMA, we propose a low complexity method of TD-SCDMA downlink synchronization detection and the performance of TD-SCDMA downlink synchronization, with different quantization word length and SNR, is designed and tested by using software simulation. Furthermore, the required minimized word length is found. We verify our algorithm by computer simulations, and the results show a good performance in a wide range of signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs).

articleTitle: Adaptive resource allocation schemes for OFDMA systems with proportional rate constraint
publicationTitle: Symposium on ICT and Energy Efficiency and Workshop on Information Theory and Security (CIICT 2012)
abstract: Considering the problem of sub-carriers and power allocation for the downlink of an orthogonal frequency division multiplexing access (OFDMA) system with proportional fairness, the paper develops an improved resource allocation algorithm for OFDMA systems with inter-carrier interference (ICI) based on genetic algorithm. The paper develops an improved water-filling algorithm at the same time. The resource allocation problem is formulated as one that maximizes the total capacity of all active users subject to certain constraint conditions, which are determined by proportional fairness, total power and bit error rate. The simulation results show that the proposed algorithms have better performance in proportional fairness, algorithm convergence and complexity of the algorithm compared to the existing methods.

articleTitle: VMSecurexec: Transparent on-access virus detection for virtual machine in the cloud
publicationTitle: Symposium on ICT and Energy Efficiency and Workshop on Information Theory and Security (CIICT 2012)
abstract: Virus detection technology is an important approach to protect host and network security. However, once the operating system (OS) is infected, anti-virus (AV) software and any other software running in it will be equally vulnerable. To address this problem, VMSecurexec, which we proposed, is designed to move on-access virus detection engine out of the target OS to another virtual machine (VM). The system firstly monitors every system call event of loading codes from an executable or shared library into memory. Then it intercepts these system call events and retrieves their parameters and return values via Second Trap mechanism. Finally, utilizing the virtual machine introspection (VMI) technique, it examines whether the binary content is malicious or not transparently. The experiments show the efficiency of out-of-VM virus detection and the moderate overhead it introduces.

articleTitle: A self-adaptive multi-objective optimization algorithm based on the Pareto's non-dominated sets
publicationTitle: Symposium on ICT and Energy Efficiency and Workshop on Information Theory and Security (CIICT 2012)
abstract: In order to improve the optimization efficiency in the multi-objective fault optimization, the self-adaptive multi-objective optimization algorithm based on the Pareto's non-dominated sets by binary tree (SMOS) are proposed in the paper. Firstly, the Self-adaptive adjustment of inertia weight is put forward to adjust the fitness function based on niche sharing mechanism. Secondly, the Pareto non-dominated sets are constructed by the binary tree to improve the optimization efficiency. Then, the SMOS algorithm is present reduce the optimized time complexity of constructed Pareto non-dominated sets when the optimized object number are larger. Meanwhile that the constructed non-dominated sets belongs the Pareto sets is proved. Finally the simulation results show when the numbers of non-dominated population are more than 5, the non-dominated efficiency can improve approximately 50%.

articleTitle: An optimal design of infinitely long period spreading sequences based on logistic mapping
publicationTitle: Symposium on ICT and Energy Efficiency and Workshop on Information Theory and Security (CIICT 2012)
abstract: Chaos is more and more used in security communication, because it is a deterministic random process in nonlinear dynamic systems. Chaotic spreading spectrum one application of Chaotic communication. As the basis, this article proposes a new optimal design of infinitely long period chaotic spreading sequences. This method optimizes the binary-quantization thresholds corresponding to different fractal parameters. This article simulates and analyzes the design results, and the results show that the method can generate a huge amount of high-performance and security chaotic spreading sequences.

articleTitle: A novel spectrum sensing technique based on diversity reception
publicationTitle: Symposium on ICT and Energy Efficiency and Workshop on Information Theory and Security (CIICT 2012)
abstract: Spectrum sensing is one of the key technologies in Cognitive Radio. A conventional approach to sensing primary user signal is using single antenna. Due to multi-path fading and shadowing effect, detection is unreliable. This can make cognitive radio susceptible to the “hidden node” problem. This paper proposes a novel spectrum sensing technique based on diversity reception by combining multi-antenna technology with energy detection. Firstly, received signals of primary users coming from every antenna are processed by diversity reception technique. Secondly, cognitive user judges the presence of primary user by energy detection. Simulation results show: Spectrum sensing technique based on diversity reception could improve reliability of energy detection and increase the detection performance significantly to primary user signal, overcoming the “hidden node” problem effectively.

articleTitle: Universal approximation of T-S fuzzy systems
publicationTitle: Symposium on ICT and Energy Efficiency and Workshop on Information Theory and Security (CIICT 2012)
abstract: The relationship between the approximation accuracy and the membership functions, the defuzzifier and number of fuzzy rule of T-S fuzzy systems are studied. According to mathematical properties of continuous function, the universal approximation properties of fuzzy mapping in only one interval are analyzed, and some related theorems are proposed and proved. Then, the sufficient conditions of the general T-S fuzzy systems with universal approximation are derived from these theorems, which helps establish the new relationship between approximation error bounds and the number of the fuzzy rules of different T-S fuzzy systems. Finally, the paper proposes some suggestions to construct T-S fuzz systems with universal approximation.

articleTitle: Thresholds of precoded (3,6) LDPC codes under iterative and maximum-likelihood decodings
publicationTitle: Symposium on ICT and Energy Efficiency and Workshop on Information Theory and Security (CIICT 2012)
abstract: The technique of precoding is recently applied to low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes by Divsalar et al, resulting in precoded LDPC codes. It is shown that precoding can improve not only the iterative decoding thresholds of regular LDPC codes but also their maximum-likelihood (ML) decoding thresholds. In this paper, we consider thresholds of precoded (3,6) LDPC codes under both iterative and ML decodings. For iterative decoding, the tool of EXIT charts is employed. With the EXIT chart, thresholds of precoded (3,6) LDPC codes with different precoding ratios are obtained. It is shown that the iterative decoding threshold is reduced with the increase of the precoding ratio until the precoding ratio reaches at 0.25. When the precoding ratio is greater than 0.25, the increase of precoding ratio may impair the iterative decoding threshold. Thus, the optimal precoding ratio under iterative decoding is revealed to be 0.25, i.e., half of the information bits are to be precoded. For ML decoding analysis, we first drive the asymptotic ensemble distance spectrum of precoded (3,6) LDPC codes. Using the derived asymptotic ensemble distance spectrum along with Divsalar's simple bound, we calculate the thresholds of precoded (3,6) LDPC codes with different precoding ratios under ML decoding. It is shown that the increase of precoding ratio always leads to an improved ML decoding threshold and thus the optimal ML decoding threshold is achieved at a precoding ratio of 0.5, i.e., all information bits are to be precoded.

articleTitle: A random sleeping depth based adaptive sleeping method in WSNs
publicationTitle: Symposium on ICT and Energy Efficiency and Workshop on Information Theory and Security (CIICT 2012)
abstract: Query tasks will lead multiple neighbouring nodes in the monitoring region to collect the target information and transmit the data synchronously in event-driven wireless sensor networks. A random sleeping depth based adaptive sleeping method is proposed to choice different sleep time randomly of the neighbouring nodes, relieve data packet collisions caused by simultaneous transmission after the end of sleeping phase and reduce the energy consumption of idle listening. The performance of the proposed mechanism and the optimization of sleep depth interval can be acquired after establishing the Markov chain model.

articleTitle: Sharing secret image with Error Correcting Codes
publicationTitle: Symposium on ICT and Energy Efficiency and Workshop on Information Theory and Security (CIICT 2012)
abstract: Secret image sharing scheme should be able to reveal the secret image when some shadows are lost, and the generated shadows should be embedded into meaningful cover images not to attract the intruder's attention. This article first proposes a novel image sharing scheme based on Error Correcting Codes. The scheme can recover the secret image reversibly by utilizing the error correcting ability of Error Correcting Codes when some shadows are lost, and won't attract the attacker's attention by embedding the shadows into ordinary cover images. The computation of the proposed scheme is less than most other schemes, and the secret image can be shared and recovered quickly. The experimental results show that the proposed scheme is feasible and effective.

articleTitle: High-stability routing protocol based on min-cost max-flow algorithm for MANET
publicationTitle: Symposium on ICT and Energy Efficiency and Workshop on Information Theory and Security (CIICT 2012)
abstract: MANET is currently a hotspot in the wireless network research domain, and the routing protocol, which is as the core technology on network layers, is particularly important. Improving the routing-stability can decrease the numbers of routing reconstruction, network delay and routing control overhead, which is the key to realize the transmission of efficient service in MANET. On the basis of defining the link-stability and the path-stability, combining with the idea of min-cost max-flow in networks, this paper puts forward the max-stability shortest-path model. Then the paper defines the percentage of the stability improvement as an evaluating indicator to do network simulations. Results of simulations show that this model can efficiently improve the routing-stability, and with the increasing of one-hop radius and node movement speed, the improvement effect of routing- stability is more obvious.

articleTitle: Audio watermarking scheme based on lifting wavelet transform
publicationTitle: Symposium on ICT and Energy Efficiency and Workshop on Information Theory and Security (CIICT 2012)
abstract: In order to improve the efficiency and performance of audio copyright protect technology, a robust blind audio watermarking scheme is proposed based on lifting wavelet transform, discrete cosine transform (DCT) and singular value decomposition (SVD) in the paper. In the algorithm, an original audio is split into equal frames and each frame is decomposed with DCT, whose coefficients are decomposed with the lifting wavelet transform. Then a singular value matrix is obtained after decomposing the approximate sub-band coefficients with singular value decomposition. At last, the watermarking information is embedded into the singular value matrix. Experimental results verifies that the proposed watermarking algorithm equips strong robustness against several kinds of attacks such as noise addition, re-sampling, re-quantization, MP3 compression, replace and so on.

articleTitle: An improved short-term public key-based broadcast authentication in wireless sensor networks
publicationTitle: Symposium on ICT and Energy Efficiency and Workshop on Information Theory and Security (CIICT 2012)
abstract: Broadcast authentication is a critical security service in sensor networks, since it allows a sender to broadcast messages to multiple nodes in a secure way. To reduce some disadvantages of a broadcast authentication scheme named ShortPK, we propose an improved broadcast authentication scheme. Our scheme uses Bloom filter for the public key distribution and authentication. The performance analysis shows our scheme can not only reduce about 40% less communication energy consumption than ShortPK, and U-ShortPK consumes less total energy than ShortPK but also simplifies the process of the public key distribution.

articleTitle: Dynamic resource allocation in relay-aided celluar OFDMA systems
publicationTitle: Symposium on ICT and Energy Efficiency and Workshop on Information Theory and Security (CIICT 2012)
abstract: In this paper, we consider the problem of joint bandwidth and power allocation for the relay aided orthogonal frequency division multiple access (OFDMA) system. A fractional frequency reuse (FFR) technique for interference mitigation in relay OFDMA cellular wireless networks is proposed based on a statistical knowledge of the user channels. The resource allocation problem is formulated as a power minimization problem, subject to meeting the target rates of all users in the network. We develop a distributed algorithm to find the globally optimal cell bandwidth allocation, user sub-carrier numbers and power allocation dynamically based on traffic demands and channel conditions. Our numerical results show that the presented solution has better performance compared to the fixed bandwidth allocation methods.

articleTitle: Iterative learning control of non-linear systems with iteration-varying control direction and reference trajectory
publicationTitle: Symposium on ICT and Energy Efficiency and Workshop on Information Theory and Security (CIICT 2012)
abstract: For a class of high order nonlinear systems with structure and non structure uncertainty which are repeatable in a finite time interval, an adaptive iterative learning control algorithm is proposed. By combining the Back stepping approach, the system replacement technique with the parameter regrouping technique, which can handle the iteration-varying control direction and iteration-varying trajectory tracking problem. A differential-difference type adaptive law and an adaptive iterative learning controller are constructed to ensure the asymptotic convergence of tracking error in the sense of square error norm on the finite interval, by introducing a Lyapunov function, a sufficient condition of the convergence of the method is given. A simulation example illustrates the feasibility of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A new design method of source-channel coding based on information and communication technology
publicationTitle: Symposium on ICT and Energy Efficiency and Workshop on Information Theory and Security (CIICT 2012)
abstract: With the fast development of the modern information and communication technology, there happens some profound transformation in the modern society, and information transfer method change quickly. A new design method for source-channel coding based on compressed sensing (CS) and low-density parity-check(LDPC) codes is proposed in the paper, which can achieve excellent performance by utilizing CS redundant information to correct LDPC decoding algorithm. Simulations show that performance of the proposed algorithm in reducing the bit-error rate is much better than that of LDPC codes.

articleTitle: An alternative proof for the secrecy capacity region of the Gaussian wiretap channel
publicationTitle: Symposium on ICT and Energy Efficiency and Workshop on Information Theory and Security (CIICT 2012)
abstract: This paper considers the problem of proof for the secrecy capacity region of the Gaussian wiretap channel. In this channel, the transmitter sends confidential messages to the legitimate receivers, which need to be kept asymptotically perfectly secret from the eavesdropper. We characterize the secrecy capacity region of this channel and give a converse proof by using the fundamental relationship between information theory and the estimation theory in the Gaussian channel, relating the derivative of the mutual information to the minimum mean-square-error (MMSE). Our proof is different from the superposition coding and the random binning. We obtain that using the relationship between MMSE and mutual information one can provide insightful and simple proofs for multiuser single antenna problems and the secrecy capacity problem, such as broadcast channel.

articleTitle: Analysis of the number of even-variable Boolean functions with maximum algebraic immunity
publicationTitle: Symposium on ICT and Energy Efficiency and Workshop on Information Theory and Security (CIICT 2012)
abstract: Algebraic Immunity has been considered as one of significant properties for Boolean functions, and possessing maximum algebraic immunity (MAI) is a necessary criteria for Boolean functions used in stream ciphers against algebraic attacks. However, for a given number of variables, the accurate number of Boolean functions with MAI is not known, and the best known bound on the number also seems weak. In this paper, we investigate the enumeration of Boolean functions with MAI, and provide a new lower bound on the number of even-variable Boolean functions with MAI, this lower bound is better than the previous ones.

articleTitle: A synchronous algorithm of network coding with hardware logic
publicationTitle: Symposium on ICT and Energy Efficiency and Workshop on Information Theory and Security (CIICT 2012)
abstract: This paper presents an efficient hardware prototype for network coding (NC). First, a packet synchronization mechanism is introduced to settle the problem of packet arriving mismatch between different incoming channels. Then a high-speed lookup-table-based circuit is designed to perform dot product over Galois Field, which forms the basic calculation unit of NC operation. Taking the speed advantage of FPGA hardware, this prototype is able to perform network coding operations within several hundred nanoseconds. Thus further studies and emulations on NC are able to be carried out upon this platform in the real network scenario.

articleTitle: Coal ASH fusion temperature model based on SVM optimized by ACO
publicationTitle: Symposium on ICT and Energy Efficiency and Workshop on Information Theory and Security (CIICT 2012)
abstract: A coal ash fusion temperature model is constructed based on support vector machine(SVM). The compositions of coal ash are employed as the inputs and the ash fusion temperature is the output. A series of improvement is made on basic ant colony optimization(ACO) and it is used to optimize the parameters of the SVM model. The coal ash fusion temperature is predicted by the ACO-optimized SVM model. Some experiments are performed to compare the predicted and the measured temperature and the results show the ACO-optimized SVM model can achieve better predicting performance. The advantages of SVM model, such as small sampling, fast computing speed and real-time processing and predicting are also displayed.

articleTitle: Spread spectrum audio information hiding algorithm based on auditory perception
publicationTitle: Symposium on ICT and Energy Efficiency and Workshop on Information Theory and Security (CIICT 2012)
abstract: To solve the problem that the auditory masking threshold curve calculated by common method has a large deviation, a new calculation method with comprehensive consideration of simultaneous and backward masking and independent calculation of masking threshold in the frequency domain point by point is proposed. The method can take full advantage of auditory masking characteristics and improve the capacity and robustness without losing good perceptual transparency. Furthermore, by adopting some measures including perceptual reshaping, in-phase modification and multi-frame superposition, a spread-spectrum-based audio information hiding algorithm resistant to desynchronization is presented. Simulation results show that the bit error rate of extracted messages is less than 1.6 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−2</sup>, that is, the algorithm is robust against common signal interferences such as desynchronization, additive noise, re-sampling and filtering.

articleTitle: Entanglement dynamcis and classical frequency spectrum in an integrable system
publicationTitle: Symposium on ICT and Energy Efficiency and Workshop on Information Theory and Security (CIICT 2012)
abstract: The role of classical dynamics in entanglement production for an integrable system is analyzed with a model of two coupled oscillators. It is found that the entanglement of an intergrable system is closely connected with the frequency of classical motion. For different classical orbits, the entanglement of the system increases with the classical frequency entropy, which can reveal the frequency spectrum of the classical motion.

articleTitle: A definition improving method for low visibility images
publicationTitle: Symposium on ICT and Energy Efficiency and Workshop on Information Theory and Security (CIICT 2012)
abstract: Aiming at improving the quality and identification of vehicle video images in different kinds of low visibility weather, a novel definition enhancement method is proposed. The RGB debased image is converted to HSV color model first, of which the value component is successively processed by histogram equalization and definition improving method based on dark channel prior, finally combined with the other components of hue and saturation as the output image. Experiment results show that the presented method can significantly enhance the contrast and the identifiable degree of different kinds of images with low visibility.

articleTitle: An adjustment method for secure label of subject based on trust evaluation
publicationTitle: Symposium on ICT and Energy Efficiency and Workshop on Information Theory and Security (CIICT 2012)
abstract: Because secure label is static in BLP model, secure label of subject is unalterable in multi-level network which is vulnerable to suffer the risk of access. This paper analyzed the character of subject in multi-level network and put forward an adjustment method for secure label of subject based on trust evaluation. The method collects evidences of access history of subject from audit systems in the same secure domain, and then evaluates trust degree about confidentiality, integrality and availability by evidences and forms current trust section of subject on onfidentiality, integrality and availability, finally secure label is adjusted by trust section for reducing risk of information system.

articleTitle: RLS algorithm for blind source separation in non-stationary environments
publicationTitle: Symposium on ICT and Energy Efficiency and Workshop on Information Theory and Security (CIICT 2012)
abstract: A new recursive least square (RLS) algorithm based on nonlinear principal component analysis (NPCA) is proposed to address the blind source separation (BSS) problem in non-stationary environment. Forgetting factor is introduced to improve the tracking ability in non-stationary environment. The Kalman filter is used to solve the NPCA problem since its outstanding tracking performance in non-stationary environments. Simulations using the real speech source signals are used to illustrate the performance of the new RLS algorithm in static and non-stationary environments. Results show that the new RLS algorithm has faster convergence rate and better tracking capacity compared with the stochastic gradient algorithm, and previous RLS algorithm.

articleTitle: An adaptive precoder and power allocation algorithm in MIMO system
publicationTitle: Symposium on ICT and Energy Efficiency and Workshop on Information Theory and Security (CIICT 2012)
abstract: A joint linear precoding and power allocation algorithm based on users' QoS is proposed for the downlink of multiuser MIMO systems. This algorithm will improve the channel capacity of the multiuser MIMO system and guarantee different user's QoS requirement at the same time. The complex problem is simplified and decomposed into three separate steps. First, transmit precoding is computed based on block diagonalization. Second, power matched with least rate requirement each user is allocated. Last, remained power is divided for all over the users in method named filling water. The simulation result shows that it will not only cancel CCI, but also but also meet the users'service requirement compared with the other schemes at the cost of little capacity lost.

articleTitle: A non-cooperative power control algorithm based on nolinear payoff for WSNs
publicationTitle: Symposium on ICT and Energy Efficiency and Workshop on Information Theory and Security (CIICT 2012)
abstract: A non-cooperative power control algorithm for wireless sensor networks is presented to choice the appropriate transmission power and satisfies the maximum requirement of network utility. Because of reducing packet collisions and increasing good put, the proposed algorithm can effectively control transmission power of the nodes and prolong network lifetime efficiency. And the existing and uniqueness of Nash equilibrium for the algorithm is also proved. Simulation results show that the power control algorithm have optimal network performance.

articleTitle: Features of off-line handwritten digit recognition based on principal curves
publicationTitle: Symposium on ICT and Energy Efficiency and Workshop on Information Theory and Security (CIICT 2012)
abstract: Firstly soft k-segments algorithm of principal curves are used to extract the structural features of training data; Secondly the classification features used for characters coarse classification and precise classification are chosen by analyzing the structural features of principal curves in detail; Finally coarse classification and precise classification are separately carried out in off-line handwritten digits recognition. The result of the experiment shows that these features have good discriminating power of similar characters and the algorithm can effectively improve the recognition rate of off-line handwritten digits. The proposed method provides a new approach to the research for off-line handwritten digits recognition.

articleTitle: Blind cooperative compressive spectrum sensing for Cognitive Radio networks
publicationTitle: Symposium on ICT and Energy Efficiency and Workshop on Information Theory and Security (CIICT 2012)
abstract: Spectrum sensing is the fundamental task in Cognitive Radio (CR). Due to the fact that signal sparsity level is usually unavailable at CR receiver, this paper presents a blind compressive spectrum sensing approach when the sparsity level is unknown. For the sake of energy saving, each CR receiver applies Compressed Sensing (CS) to achieve less sub-Nyquist rate sample rates in order to reduce measurement number in the proposed algorithm. Then, it finds reconstruction information for detection without degrading the whole performance, for sparisty level information is not required in the detection process. Finally, simulation results are presented to testify the proposed algorithm's effectiveness in the reduction of the processed data, hence energy saving could be achieved.

articleTitle: A reliable routing organization method in heterogeneous sensor network
publicationTitle: Symposium on ICT and Energy Efficiency and Workshop on Information Theory and Security (CIICT 2012)
abstract: The heterogeneous sensor network is a widespread network of sensors in our life. In the heterogeneous sensor network consisting of ordinary nodes and senior nodes, senior nodes are used for clustering-head to collect and transmit information to base station, the reliability of the senior nodes impact on the reliability of the whole network. In order to improve the reliability of the senior nodes puts forward senior nodes to be classified into common senior nodes and candidate senior nodes. When common senior nodes malfunction, candidate senior nodes with mobile function will substitute common senior nodes to perform work. Another, common senior nodes are organized into double-loop structure to enhance running reliability. The simulation shows that this organization method can improve energy efficiency, reduce imbalance energy consumption.

articleTitle: Direct path interference suppression algorithm of bistatic sonar system based on spatial smoothing
publicationTitle: Symposium on ICT and Energy Efficiency and Workshop on Information Theory and Security (CIICT 2012)
abstract: In the system of bistatic sonar, the direct path interference (DPI) can't be suppressed in the time and frequency fields because the DPI is highly correlated with the target signals. A suppression algorithm based on adaptive spatial smoothing is put forward in the spatial field. In the case of uniform linear array, this algorithm first establishes the model of adaptive beam former to get the optimal weighted vector, then applies the vector to spatial smoothing beam form. Thus the correlativity between DPI and target signal is eliminated quite well to ensure the effect of DPI suppression. The results of simulation and experiments show that the algorithm is more effective than common spatial smoothing beam form algorithms to eliminate DPI.

articleTitle: A dynamic model in P2P Services Environment for accurate and robust trust evaluations
publicationTitle: Symposium on ICT and Energy Efficiency and Workshop on Information Theory and Security (CIICT 2012)
abstract: A three-dimension dynamic trust model is proposed in this paper for trust management in P2P Services Environment. The main contributions include: presenting a three-dimension model to calculate the peer's initial trust, direct trust and recommended trust; constructing a Gauss-bar function to evaluate the comparability of service satisfaction; distinguishing the reliability of information from different peers including friends, neighbors, stranger and blacklist peers; setting some parameters in computing recommendation trust, such as recommendation consistency, recommendation accuracy, and recommendation errors, which let trust evaluation become more natural and precise, and so on. Theoretic analysis and simulations show that the proposed trust model is more precise and more robust than previous works.

articleTitle: Adaptive repetitive control for nonlinear systems with time-varying parameters uncertainty
publicationTitle: Symposium on ICT and Energy Efficiency and Workshop on Information Theory and Security (CIICT 2012)
abstract: A design approach to the adaptive learning controller is proposed for a class of high-order nonlinear systems with time-varying and time-invariant parameters by combining the Backstepping technique with the pointwise integral mechanism. It can be applied in the time-varying parametric uncertainty systems with unknown compact set, rapid time-varying, periodic and only the prior knowledge is the periodicity. A periodic mixed adaptive law and an adaptive control law are constructed to ensure the asymptotic convergence of the tracking error in the sense of square error norm. And a sufficient condition of the convergence of the method is also given. A simulation example illustrates the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: Optimal placement of virtual machines with different placement constraints in IAAS clouds
publicationTitle: Symposium on ICT and Energy Efficiency and Workshop on Information Theory and Security (CIICT 2012)
abstract: There has been much research activity recently in relation to the optimal placement of virtual machines (VMs) on physical servers. Usually the objective is to consolidate the VMs on servers for energy-saving purposes in a cloud environment. In this paper, we study the problem of optimizing the allocation of VMs having different placement constraints (e.g., security and anti-collocation) and characteristics (e.g., memory and disk capacity), given a set of physical hosts with known specifications, in order to achieve the objective of maximizing the cloud provider's revenue. This is an important resource allocation problem in data centers. Our approach is based on the formulation of the problem as an integer linear programming (ILP) problem. The ILP model produces an optimal placement for VMs with different placement constraints. Given a model of VM placement constraints, offered resources and required VM sets, the model devises a plan to allocate VMs to servers in a way that maximizes revenue, having due regard both to customer requirements and server capacities. The performance of the algorithms is evaluated by means of numerical experiments. Experiments suggest that this model and its associated solution strategy is practical for the offline development of VM-to-server allocation plans given a typical mix of customer demands for virtualized computing resources in small or medium data centers.

articleTitle: Network real-time threat awareness and analysis based on attack state transition graph
publicationTitle: Symposium on ICT and Energy Efficiency and Workshop on Information Theory and Security (CIICT 2012)
abstract: In order to comprehend and accurately estimate the current network security situation to preferably guide dynamic defense, an awareness and analysis method for network real-time threats is proposed. The method recognizes current real-time threats and predicts subsequent threats by modelling attack scenario and simulating intrusion state transferring. The threat awareness model is constructed with Expanded Finite-State Automata, which is defined as Attack State Transition Graph and Real-Time Attack State Graph. Based on the former all possible intruding paths and state transformation can be illustrated, and based on the latter really happening threats and intruding path are described. Then a threat awareness algorithm is presented based on the above model. With this algorithm, various kinds of invalid threats are filtered, current valid threats are obtained by correlating dynamic alarms with static attack scenario. Further, combining Attack State Transition Graph with Real-Time Attack State Graph, subsequent threat and possible threat path is identified and intrusion target is predicted. Finally the results of experiment in a simulated network verify the feasibility and validity of the model and algorithm. Therefore, it provides a novel solution to recognize and analyze network security situation.

articleTitle: An enhanced remote mutual authentication scheme using smart cards
publicationTitle: Symposium on ICT and Energy Efficiency and Workshop on Information Theory and Security (CIICT 2012)
abstract: Mutual authentication is a process or technology in which both entities in a communications link authenticate each other before conducting any business. It is gaining acceptance as a tool that can minimize the risk of online fraud in e-commerce and other network application. Recently, Wang et al. proposed an efficient remote authentication scheme using smart cards. They claimed that the scheme can withstand guessing attack, forgery attack, denial of service attack and is easily realized in the practical resource-limited environment. However, we point out that Wang et al.'s scheme suffers from parallel session attack and replay attack. Furthermore, we propose an enhanced remote mutual authentication scheme to eliminate all identified security flaws in the aforementioned scheme.

articleTitle: Differential addition on Jacobi quartic curves
publicationTitle: Symposium on ICT and Energy Efficiency and Workshop on Information Theory and Security (CIICT 2012)
abstract: The Jacobi quartic curve is a representation of an elliptic curve different from the usual Weierstrass equation. To achieve a faster algorithm, recent works use up to 7 coordinates to represent a single point. In this paper, we present differential addition formulas on Jacobi quartic curves, and it only needs 2 coordinates for every point. Analysis shows that our algorithm provides the competitive speed with existent methods, but it needs less memory. So our algorithm is more suitable to resource constrained environments, such as smart card and mobile phone.

articleTitle: Phase modulation-enabled transmission performance improvement and parameter-relaxation of DACS/ADCS in SMF-based IMDD optical OFDM systems
publicationTitle: Symposium on ICT and Energy Efficiency and Workshop on Information Theory and Security (CIICT 2012)
abstract: Adaptively modulated optical orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (AMOOFDM) using phase modulation (PM) (AMOOFDM-PM) is proposed and theoretically explored, for the first time, in intensity modulation and direct detection (IMDD) single-mode fibre systems. AMOOFDM-PM utilises an electrical OFDM signal to modulate the phase of a RF carrier prior to performing optical intensity modulation. Compared to conventional AMOOFDM based on amplitude modulation, AMOOFDM-PM can not only significantly lower the minimum requirements on quantization bits and sampling rates of digital-to-analogue /analogue-to-digital converters, but also simultaneously considerably improves the signal transmission performance. In addition, AMOOFDM-PM also shows excellent system flexibility and performance robustness to variations in transmission link characteristics.

articleTitle: Smart energy management for off-grid hybrid sites in telecoms
publicationTitle: Symposium on ICT and Energy Efficiency and Workshop on Information Theory and Security (CIICT 2012)
abstract: Hybrid power infrastructure is often viewed as an alternative system configuration for off-grid telecom base stations. These systems are used to reduce the fuel consumption of diesel generator sites and often rely on wind or solar to supplement some of the power to the load. The ability of a site to use the renewable energy efficiently becomes more critical on sites where the quality of the wind or solar resource is poor or highly variable. The long term and short term effects of wind and solar power contributions to the system are demonstrated using historical wind speed/solar irradiation data over a 3 year period. A feasible approach is proposed to improve the efficiency of the system by analysing the rate of change of the renewable energy source(s). Using several successive measurements, the battery charging system can be restrained temporarily to allow for the initial stages of diurnal weather patterns. These patterns may later negate the need for the charging cycle which can result in wasted power should a renewable power source increase its power output during a generator charging cycle.
